past_paper_mcqs.stem_text:
If a body of mass $10\text{ kg}$ is placed on the surface of the Earth, then the pull of the Earth on the body will be
(Note: The value of acceleration due to gravity is $9.8\text{ m/s}^2$.)
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: The pull of Earth on a body is its weight $W = mg = 10\text{ kg} \times 9.8\text{ m/s}^2 = 98\text{ N}$.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: Two forces ($9\text{ N}$ and $12\text{ N}$) act at the right angle at point O, as shown in the given figure. What will be the magnitude and direction of the resultant force?
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: Magnitude $R = \sqrt{9^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{81 + 144} = \sqrt{225} = 15\text{ N}$. By vector addition (head-to-tail / parallelogram law), the resultant lies along OQ.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: A sports racing car is made stable by
options: D. lowering its centre of gravity.
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: Lowering the centre of gravity increases stability, preventing the car from tipping over during sharp turns.

crqs.question: Describe the THREE states of equilibrium on the basis of the centre of gravity and give one daily-life example of each.
crqs.answer: 1. Stable equilibrium: CoG rises on slight displacement and body returns to original position (e.g., book lying flat on a table). 2. Unstable equilibrium: CoG lowers on displacement and body topples (e.g., pencil balanced on its tip). 3. Neutral equilibrium: CoG height remains unchanged on displacement (e.g., rolling ball on a horizontal floor).
crqs.source: AKU-EB SSC-I 2025 Annual Paper II Q.2 & Model Paper II Q.2

erqs.question: State the principle of moments and explain the two conditions required for a rigid body to remain in complete equilibrium.
erqs.answer: Principle of moments: Sum of clockwise moments about a pivot equals sum of anticlockwise moments. Conditions of equilibrium: First condition ΣF = 0 (no linear acceleration); Second condition Στ = 0 (no angular acceleration).

numericals.problem: A uniform metre rule is pivoted at the 50 cm mark. A 4 N weight hangs at the 20 cm mark. Where should a 6 N weight be suspended to balance the rule horizontally?
numericals.solution: Anticlockwise moment = 4 N × (50 - 20) cm = 120 N·cm. For balance, 6 N × d₂ = 120 N·cm => d₂ = 20 cm to the right of pivot (at the 70 cm mark).
